rationale: No controlled clinical study isolates ground saffron for examiner-rated muscle rigidity severity in Parkinson disease. A randomized Tehran Parkinson trial of unspecified saffron capsules (n=52; DOI10.1016/j.hermed.2024.100968) found an inconclusive total MDS-UPDRS Part III contrast (p=.424) with no separate rigidity item; uncontrolled supplement charts and vegetarian menus do not isolate saffron; and injected safranal, crocin, or crocetinate rodent catalepsy assays are remote proxies. Crocetin and crocetinate models distinguish isolated preparations from ground saffron. The review's structural rigidity refers to the molecule. Xi and Qian and the historical compendium add provenance with no Parkinson muscle-rigidity measurement. The Rao fly study compared saffron extract and isolated crocin and reported favorable locomotor readouts. Different preparations and fly outcomes do not measure examiner-rated rigidity after ground saffron in people. The Isfahan Sargol protocol separately planned MDS-UPDRS motor examinations. No isolated rigidity result was accessible in the published outcomes. The exact comparison remains open.

The Isfahan trial directly assessed Parkinson fatigue after swallowing tablets containing dried Sargol stigma powder versus placebo. The adjusted difference was −9.20 points (95% CI −13.76 to −4.65), favoring less fatigue. The primary sample-size calculation was for a biomarker. The original registry and September 2024 journal submission omit the standalone fatigue scale. It first appears in the archived July 2025 registry revision and August 9, 2025 journal R1, both after the outcome manuscript was received. The fixed preparation and single eligible Parkinson trial keep the direction provisional. Non-Parkinson extract comparisons are mixed or inconclusive. The Ashtiani syrup lacks a control and its initial fatigue mean exceeds the scale range described in its own methods. The matched Parkinson sample supports easing and opposes the frozen worsening claim. Internal outcome-selection and study completion dates and independent Parkinson fatigue comparisons remain open. The original fibromyalgia extract-versus-duloxetine report supplies an inconclusive Global Fatigue Index contrast with a wide interval. Its active comparator and non-Parkinson population limit transfer. Three Alzheimer trials report sparse fatigue adverse-event counts after stigma extract, and the perimenopausal SF-36 energy/fatigue comparison is inconclusive. Each remains contextual to the direct Parkinson fatigue measurement. The separate standardized-extract trial reports a favorable broad sleep-related impairment result with a tiredness item. No fatigue-specific estimate is reported, and the registration excludes Parkinson disease.

A powder capsule pilot showed inconclusively slower upper-gut transit. Piperine and extract experiments give mixed bowel proxies. The human mixed-tablet pilot has conflicting counts and no controls. Cracked black pepper and clinical Parkinson constipation remain unresolved. Related cultural/experiential records (1) provide uncontrolled context without changing the open efficacy rating. The autism review mentions constipation as clinical context and piperine in a separate developmental-mouse model. The primary piperine abstract has no constipation endpoint. No cracked-black-pepper Parkinson result. A separate uncontrolled multi-herb study with black pepper and senna reports within-person improvement. The effect of cracked black pepper remains undefined.

Nonoral grapeseed sleep comparisons and healthy-adult oil cookies provided no clinical Parkinson insomnia outcome. A planned insomnia trial names a linoleic-acid cookie without identifying the oil. A separate oral proanthocyanidin-extract pilot reports within-arm improvement in menopause and gives no placebo-relative insomnia contrast in the available abstract. This preparation differs from refined grapeseed oil.

The MPTP mouse study found longer rotarod retention on day 20 after aqueous cumin fruit extract given before toxin exposure. Day 5 was inconclusive and the paper gives conflicting animal counts. This observed benefit concerns prevention and model coordination. The heated spice chemistry varies by preparation, with no measured bridge to the tested extract or a standalone clinical postural-instability result. The Parkinson food survey records cumin intake without a postural estimate. Human trials and customary source checks do not furnish a separate outcome after toasted culinary cumin.
